messages:
anya: Heads-up — I started intake for a community model we want to evaluate for a partner pilot: pegasusx/7b (HF). Need quick legal check + quant/eval plan before we proceed. ping @rachel @mike @sanjay

mike: link + license snippet pls, and what's the target workload? summarization only? chat?

anya: https://huggingface.co/pegasusx/7b — model_card shows: "This model is released under CC-BY-NC-4.0. Commercial use is prohibited without permission." Also notes weights derived from mixed third-party datasets. Workload = abstractive summarization + some prompt-based summarization in partner app (paid).

legal-bot: Automated scan -> license: CC-BY-NC-4.0. FLAG: non-commercial clause present. Recommend manual legal review. No export-control flag detected from metadata; confirm training data provenance.

rachel: Quick take: CC-BY-NC means we cannot include the model in our hosted paid API or use it in revenue-generating pilots without explicit permission from the rights holder. Dedicated/private deployments for customers don't magically make it allowed if the end use is commercial. We need to ask author for a commercial license or choose a permissive alternative.

anya: Ugh — partner expects a paid pilot. Is there any temporary path (bench-only) we can do while legal chases license?

rachel: Yes — we can do internal benchmarking and offline evals in our sandbox infra, labelled "evaluation only" and not exposed to partner. Do NOT expose model in hosted or paid environments until we get authorization.

mike: Ok — I'll start local bring-up and quant experiments in an isolated env. Proposed plan:
- baseline eval (XSum ROUGE, CNN/DM)
- instruction/following tests (20 prompts)
- hallucination/regression suite (our eval harness)
- quant pipeline: run GPTQ q4_0 and a PTQ int8 variant, measure delta on ROUGE and EM

Example run commands I'll use:
```
# quantize
python tools/quantize.py --model pegasusx/7b --method q4_0 --out /tmp/pegasusx-q4
# eval
python eval/summarize.py --model /tmp/pegasusx-q4 --dataset xsum --metrics rouge
```

mike: Goal thresholds: quality drop <= 2.0 ROUGE-1 relative to fp16 for q4_0; if larger, try hybrid q4/fp16 or different calibration. Latency target for 7B on a single A100-40: p99 < 800 ms for 512-token summary (batch=1).

sanjay: infra questions: estimated model size + GPU memory footprint? expected QPS for pilot? also need to know if we'll use offload or single-GPU.

anya: rough numbers from a quick load: ~13GB fp16 checkpoint; loaded with some optimizer state stripped. Baseline testing done on A100-40 with kv-cache — fits in 48GB. Pilot QPS ~0.3 r/s per instance, burst to 1. We'll prefer single-GPU; can consider CPU offload if quant reduces memory.

infra-bot: Suggest config: max_batch_tokens=2048, max_sequence=1024, request_timeout 30s. Add fallback routes to smaller permissive model. Recommend canary rollout and traffic shaping if we ever host.

liz: Product note — partner is okay to wait for license, but timeline matters (2 weeks). They asked us to prioritize if legal clearance possible quickly. Any chance of a commercial license buyout?

rachel: I'll reach out to model author today to request commercial licensing terms & attribution requirements. I'll CC partner contact if author requests negotiation. For now: HOLD on any externally visible deployments.

mike: small status update — started quant run on local node. Initial quick results (toy run, q4_0):
```
fp16 xsum rouge-1: 41.2
q4_0 xsum rouge-1: 40.8  (delta -0.4)
int8 ptq xsum rouge-1: 37.4  (delta -3.8)
```
q4 looks promising; int8 PTQ lost too much. I'll run full eval with 3 seeds and compute mean/std.

anya: great — please log full eval artifacts to s3 bucket redwood-model-evals/pegasusx/7b/2026-03-20 and link them in the ticket.

rachel: Created JIRA INF-4217 to track licensing + bringup: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4217 — assigned to me (legal) and mike (eval). Do not host until license cleared.

anya: Checklist for next steps (for visibility):
1) Legal: confirm commercial license OR get written permission (rachel)
2) ML: full eval suite + quant experiments + regression alerts (mike)
3) Infra: memory/cost perf numbers + canary plan (sanjay)
4) Product: confirm partner payment terms & timeline (liz)
5) Ops: add model gate entry + rollout policy if approved (INF ticket)

mike: I'll update INF-4217 with eval artifacts, perf matrix (latency, mem, cost-est), and quant recommendations (q4_0 recommended; int8 not ready).

rachel: I'll ping author today and post back here. ETA 3 business days. If author declines commercial terms, we can propose a swap to a permissive model or explore paid license.

anya: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the canonical intake. I'll avoid spinning up any hosted endpoints until we get an explicit thumbs-up from legal. :white_check_mark: 

sanjay: noted. once legal clears, we'll need an infra runbook for deployment: instance type, autoscale policy, fallback model id, and rollback triggers.

mike: noted — will draft runbook and perf dashboard config (Grafana links) and attach to INF-4217.

rachel: update — emailed author + legal contact at 11:12am. Will post reply thread here when I hear back.

anya: OK — thread pinned for visibility.
